title: Dense GEMM
summary: One matrix multiply: an activation block of m tokens times a weight matrix.
description: Every linear layer in a transformer is a dense GEMM: QKV and output projections, dense MLPs, the LM head. m is the number of tokens in the batch; n and k come from the weight shape. Backends that share this table differ in how the weight is laid out and which library dispatches the multiply, and the simulator picks the fastest measured backend per shape.
formula: C[m, n] = A[m, k] · B[k, n]
GB/s = (m·k + k·n + m·n) · bytes per element / time

m.meaning: Rows of the activation: tokens in the batch.

dtype.meaning: Element type of A and B. fp8_e4m3 writes bf16 output.

method: GPU kernel time from CUPTI activity records, averaged over repeated launches in one capture. The L2 cache is flushed before each launch, so the numbers are cold-cache times. Blackwell can split one logical GEMM into overlapping launches; those are counted once, by the time the GPU is busy.
caveats: Inputs are random normal tensors, so data-dependent effects such as sparsity are not measured.
torch and torch_linear compute the same product. They are separate rows because the weight layout changes which cuBLAS kernel runs.

torch.summary: torch.mm on a contiguous right-hand side.

torch_linear.summary: F.linear with the (n, k) weight layout used by vLLM and Transformers.

torch_linear_vllm.summary: The same F.linear call, run in vLLM's pinned environment.

sglang_bf16_auto.summary: SGLang's production BF16 dispatch with bf16_gemm_backend='auto' (CuTe DSL on SM100).

sglang_fused_a_auto.summary: SGLang's fused-A GEMM dispatch, for 16 tokens or fewer, on SM100.

deepgemm.summary: DeepGEMM FP8 dense kernel: fp8 in, bf16 out.

reference.note: The torch backend is its own reference: the measured call is torch.mm(a, b).
